<p class="axis-note radar-note">Outer is better on every axis; the overlaps are complementary, not a ranking; italic axes are qualitative scores (author's judgement); hover or tap an axis for its meaning.</p>
<p class="axis-note radar-note radar-caption-control">NVIDIA Warp gives you near-total control of every kernel, short of raw CUDA. raptor takes that control over on purpose, and that is where its speed on uneven batches comes from.</p>
<details class="radar-data radar-howto"><summary>How to read this radar</summary><p class="axis-note radar-note">Each measured axis is stretched over its own best-to-worst range, so ring labels differ per axis (compile time: fixed, 0.1 s to 100 s; code size: at least 4x). Axes are ordered so each tool's strengths sit together, so read the axes, not the area.</p><p class="axis-note radar-note">Qualitative axes are not measurements: hollow markers, a linear scale, and no marker where a tool has no reading. A hollow marker on compile time is the tool's simple-kernel time. The hover panel has each axis's full wording.</p><ul class="radar-howto-list"><li><strong>Tensor workloads</strong>: 5 = dense array maths, batched linear algebra and convolutions are its home ground.</li><li><strong>Array-style programming</strong>: 5 = the whole-array expression is the programming model.</li><li><strong>Half precision and below</strong>: 5 = FP16, BF16, FP8, FP4 and tensor cores are first-class paths.</li><li><strong>Low-level control</strong>: 5 = you write what each thread does and how it is launched.</li><li><strong>Single-thread abstraction</strong>: 5 = you write one sample and nothing else.</li><li><strong>Differentiable kernels</strong>: 5 = derivatives are built in for every kernel written in the tool.</li><li><strong>Works with your arrays</strong>: 5 = zero-copy exchange with other frameworks is the norm.</li><li><strong>Deploy outside Python</strong>: 5 = a compiled artefact any program can load.</li><li><strong>Extensibility</strong>: 5 = a documented plugin path across many targets.</li></ul><p class="axis-note radar-note"><a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, in the full tables</a>.</p></details>

<p class="axis-note radar-note">Outer is better on every axis; the overlaps are complementary, not a ranking; italic axes are qualitative scores (author's judgement); hover or tap an axis for its meaning.</p>
<p class="axis-note radar-note radar-caption-control">NVIDIA Warp gives you near-total control of every kernel, short of raw CUDA. raptor takes that control over on purpose, and that is where its speed on uneven batches comes from.</p>
<details class="radar-data radar-howto"><summary>How to read this radar</summary><p class="axis-note radar-note">Each measured axis is stretched over its own best-to-worst range, so ring labels differ per axis (compile time: fixed, 0.1 s to 100 s; code size: at least 4x). Axes are ordered so each tool's strengths sit together, so read the axes, not the area.</p><p class="axis-note radar-note">Qualitative axes are not measurements: hollow markers, a linear scale, and no marker where a tool has no reading. A hollow marker on compile time is the tool's simple-kernel time. The hover panel has each axis's full wording.</p><ul class="radar-howto-list"><li><strong>Tensor workloads</strong>: 5 = dense array maths, batched linear algebra and convolutions are its home ground.</li><li><strong>Array-style programming</strong>: 5 = the whole-array expression is the programming model.</li><li><strong>Half precision and below</strong>: 5 = FP16, BF16, FP8, FP4 and tensor cores are first-class paths.</li><li><strong>Low-level control</strong>: 5 = you write what each thread does and how it is launched.</li><li><strong>Single-thread abstraction</strong>: 5 = you write one sample and nothing else.</li><li><strong>Differentiable kernels</strong>: 5 = derivatives are built in for every kernel written in the tool.</li><li><strong>Works with your arrays</strong>: 5 = zero-copy exchange with other frameworks is the norm.</li><li><strong>Deploy outside Python</strong>: 5 = a compiled artefact any program can load.</li><li><strong>Extensibility</strong>: 5 = a documented plugin path across many targets.</li></ul><p class="axis-note radar-note"><a href="https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html">Every number, in the full tables</a>.</p></details>
